Hi Jordan — great conversation earlier, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the technical deep dive: 

Recap (30-min discovery)
- High-level goal: evaluate Redwood for low-latency inference serving for NovoHealth analytics pipelines (privacy-sensitive PHI workloads).
- Primary success criteria: sub-150ms 1k-token p95 for batched requests; SOC-2 aligned controls; predictable monthly committed throughput.
- Stakeholders: Jordan Miller (product), Samantha Lee (platform/infra), Dr. Patel (data/compliance) — please confirm I captured everyone.

Proposed next step: 60–90 minute technical deep dive / demo with our infra engineer + solutions lead. To accommodate your global engineering team, I put together three rotating-window options (each would be implemented as a weekly rota so different regions can join on a repeating cadence):

Option A — Americas-first rotation (weekly)
- Week 1: Tue 10:00 PDT / 13:00 EDT (US friendly)
- Week 2: Tue 17:00 BST / 18:00 CEST (EU friendly)
- Week 3: Wed 09:00 AEST / 11:00 NZT (APAC friendly)

Option B — EU-balanced rotation (preferred if your technical leads are EU-based)
- Week 1: Wed 14:00 BST / 15:00 CEST (EU)
- Week 2: Thu 08:00 PDT / 11:00 EDT (US)
- Week 3: Thu 16:00 AEST / 18:00 NZT (APAC)

Option C — APAC-first rotation (if platform team is APAC-centric)
- Week 1: Mon 09:30 AEST (APAC)
- Week 2: Mon 17:00 BST / 18:00 CEST (EU)
- Week 3: Tue 10:00 PDT / 13:00 EDT (US)

A few logistics items:
- We can cap attendance to your core infra and product engineers to keep it focused (60–90m).
- We’ll record and share notes + a short eval checklist.
- Attachment: discovery-notes-novohealth-20260804.pdf with our notes from today.

Please reply with the option you prefer (A/B/C) and a couple of concrete time slots for the first meeting this or next week. If helpful, I can send a Calendly with rotating-slot options that automatically proposes the three-week cadence.

Thanks — looking forward to aligning calendars.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
